about: Mutants of compiler/check/expr, expression types after the Go checker's Info.Types (capstone S3d). The corpus agreement (TestCompilerExprAgreesWithChecker) or the seeded property (TestCompilerExprProperty) kills each: every one makes the Ergo side type an expression otherwise than the Go checker.

mutants.name: const-default-in-context
mutants.from: if fits { some(e.T) } else { None }
mutants.to: if fits { constType(s, k, t, x, Free) } else { None }
mutants.rule: A constant takes the type its context assigns it to, not its default.

mutants.name: signed-literal-recorded
mutants.rule: A signed literal is one constant: its literal has no type of its own.

mutants.name: block-value-defaulted
mutants.from: expr(s, k, t, syntax.ExprStmtOf(tr, st).X, Unsure)
mutants.to: expr(s, k, t, syntax.ExprStmtOf(tr, st).X, Free)
mutants.rule: A block's final expression is its value, whose context decides a constant's type.

mutants.name: case-patterns-typed
mutants.from:
patterns(s, k, t, cc.List)
		stmts(s, k, t, cc.Body)
mutants.to:
patterns(s, k, t, cc.List)
		walk(s, k, t, x)
mutants.rule: A case's list is patterns, which have no expression types.

mutants.name: site-kept
mutants.from: np > 0 && n == np-1 && isCallSite(s, k, ops[np-1])
mutants.to: false && np > 0 && n == np-1 && isCallSite(s, k, ops[np-1])
mutants.rule: A callee whose CallSite the call leaves out has the siteless type.

mutants.name: wired-recorded
mutants.rule: An instance whose wired[T] the pass does not expand is not typed.

mutants.name: emptied-fails-recorded
mutants.rule: An instance whose written fails row its arguments empty keeps the written fails, which the pool does not hold: it is not typed.

mutants.name: lit-rows-assumed
mutants.from: let errs = if writesErrors(p, ft) { some(ops[n-2]) } else { closedRow(*s, expected, 2) }
mutants.to: let errs = if writesErrors(p, ft) || true { some(ops[n-2]) } else { closedRow(*s, expected, 2) }
mutants.rule: A function literal's unwritten fails row is its context's or its body's, never assumed empty.

mutants.name: address-unwrapped
mutants.from: some(store.TPointer(s, xt.Value))
mutants.to: some(store.TSlice(s, xt.Value))
mutants.rule: &x is a pointer to x's type.

mutants.name: field-unsubstituted
mutants.from: return some(store.TSubst(s, fd.T, targs))
mutants.to: return some(store.TSubst(s, fd.T, targs[0:0]))
mutants.rule: A generic record's field has its type with the record's type arguments.

mutants.name: range-key-element
mutants.from: key = some(store.TBasic(s, bInt))
mutants.to: key = some(ops[len(ops)-1])
mutants.rule: A range over a slice gives an int index, then the element.

mutants.name: subst-nests-rows
mutants.from: if int(Key(*p, ops[i]).k) == tParam && int(Key(*p, o).k) == tRow {
mutants.to: if false && int(Key(*p, ops[i]).k) == tParam && int(Key(*p, o).k) == tRow {
mutants.rule: A row parameter bound to a row splices its elements into the row it stands in: rows do not nest.

mutants.name: fn-lookup-scan
mutants.from:
t.steps = t.steps + 1
	FnAt(k, at)
mutants.rule: A declaration lookup reads one slot: typing an expression never scans the package.

mutants.name: row-in-type-bound
mutants.from:
// where Go's is the argument: the call is left uninferred.
			return false
mutants.to:
// where Go's is the argument: the call is left uninferred.
			return true
mutants.rule: A row parameter met in a type position leaves the call uninferred.

mutants.name: import-alias-qualifier
mutants.from: if f.Path == path && f.Name == name && (f.Qual == own || f.Qual == "-") {
mutants.to: if f.Path == path && f.Name == name && (true || f.Qual == own || f.Qual == "-") {
mutants.rule: An import's generic type is ported only to an entry the printer qualifies with the package's own name, as the Go checker prints it.

mutants.name: imported-field-unsubstituted
mutants.from: let u = store.TSubst(s, p.Value, targs)
mutants.to: let u = p.Value
mutants.rule: An import's generic record's field has its type with the record's type arguments.

mutants.name: imported-generic-value
mutants.from: return if len(f.Value.Params) == 0 { some(f.Value.Sig) } else { None }
mutants.to: return some(f.Value.Sig)
mutants.rule: An import's generic function named without a call has its instance's type, which the selector alone does not give: it is not typed.

mutants.name: imported-call-named-by-selector
mutants.from:
case syntax.SelectorExpr as se:
			se.Sel
		case _:
			fun
mutants.to:
case syntax.SelectorExpr as se:
			fun
		case _:
			fun
mutants.rule: A call of an import's generic function is named by its selector's name, as the Go checker's call is.

mutants.name: port-sig-rows-swapped
mutants.from: return some(store.TSig(s, ops[0:n-3], ops[n-3], ops[n-2], ops[n-1]))
mutants.to: return some(store.TSig(s, ops[0:n-3], ops[n-3], ops[n-1], ops[n-2]))
mutants.rule: A ported signature keeps its fails row and its needs row apart.

mutants.name: deps-not-frozen
mutants.from: f = store.Freeze(d.S)
mutants.to: f = f
mutants.rule: The package binds against its imports' frozen stores, so its selectors name their declarations.

mutants.name: foreign-by-name-only
mutants.from: if f.Path == path && f.Name == name {
mutants.to: if f.Name == name {
mutants.rule: An import's type is the foreign entry of its own package, not another package's type of that name.
